reasons: Section 24 as cited does meet the preferred position: 24.1 gives Customer an unconditional affiliate/M&A successor assignment right (notice only), 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment, delegation and change-of-control transfer to a reasonable-consent standard with a competitor bar, 24.3 sets a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld standard, and 24.4 expressly negates any Vendor termination, suspension, repricing or fee-acceleration right on Customer's change of control.
No walk-away features (blanket Customer assignment ban, Vendor CoC termination or re-pricing right) appear in the cited text, so a deviation finding would be over-flagging.

Consistent with a compliant claim, no redline or comment was proposed and the rendered text is unchanged from the original paragraphs; the deterministic check confirming the successor/affiliate carve-out is satisfied.

Only immaterial gaps versus preferred wording (the competitor bar is qualified by 'without Customer's consent' rather than absolute), which the playbook directs to be noted in the rationale rather than redlined.
